gloss: right of residence; right to live somewhere

definitions.gloss: right of residence; right to live somewhere
definitions.explanation: The legal right to reside in a particular place, whether in a specific property or in a country.

examples.japanese: {居住権|きょじゅうけん}は{法律|ほうりつ}で{守|まも}られている。
examples.english: The right of residence is protected by law.

examples.japanese: {配偶者|はいぐうしゃ}には{居住権|きょじゅうけん}が{認|みと}められる。
examples.english: The spouse is granted the right of residence.

examples.japanese: {相続|そうぞく}の{際|さい}に{居住権|きょじゅうけん}をめぐって{家族|かぞく}の{間|あいだ}で{争|あらそ}いが{起|お}きることがある。
examples.english: Disputes can arise among family members over the right of residence during inheritance proceedings.

notes:
A compound of {居住|きょじゅう} (residence/dwelling) and {権|けん} (right). In Japanese law, the {配偶者|はいぐうしゃ}{居住権|きょじゅうけん} (spouse's right of residence) was formally established in 2020 as part of civil code reforms, allowing a surviving spouse to continue living in their home even after inheritance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {居住権|きょじゅうけん}を{認|みと}める — to grant/recognize the right of residence
- {居住権|きょじゅうけん}を{主張|しゅちょう}する — to assert one's right of residence
- {配偶者|はいぐうしゃ}{居住権|きょじゅうけん} — spouse's right of residence
- {永住権|えいじゅうけん} — permanent residency (related but broader concept)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {永住権|えいじゅうけん} — permanent residency (specifically the right to live permanently in a country)
- {居住|きょじゅう}の{自由|じゆう} — freedom of residence (a constitutional right to choose where to live)
